verdict.rationale: Gmail's own docs say you can use Gmail offline to read, search and reply without a connection. Messages sent offline go to an Outbox and are sent automatically when you reconnect. Only outgoing mail is documented as syncing, so whether other offline changes reconcile on reconnect is unproven. missing for 10: documented sync of non-send offline changes (read state, labels, archive/delete) on reconnect, explicit coverage of composing new messages (not just replies) offline, independent or hands-on corroboration of offline reliability.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can read, search, and write email offline, with changes syncing when I reconnect

citations.quote: You can use Gmail offline to read, search, and reply to messages without an internet connection.
If you send a message offline, it's saved in a new "Outbox" folder. If you connect to the internet, the message is sent automatically.
